Implement a throttled buffering mechanism for the live output stream in the shell tool to manage high-frequency command outputs effectively. Ensure the first output chunk is displayed immediately, while subsequent chunks are batched and delivered at most once per update interval. Maintain a bounded buffer to prevent excessive memory usage.

*   Export the constant `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` from `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`.
    *   This constant defines the maximum number of characters to retain in the live output buffer.

*   Display the first text chunk immediately upon arrival by calling `updateOutput` without delay.

*   Accumulate subsequent text chunks arriving within `OUTPUT_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` in a buffer.
    *   Do not forward these chunks to `updateOutput` immediately.

*   Flush any accumulated text output when a command exits by calling `updateOutput` before the execution promise resolves.

*   Ensure the text buffer for live display does not exceed `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` characters.
    *   Retain only the trailing `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` characters, discarding older content.
    *   If truncation falls on a low surrogate code unit (0xDC00–0xDFFF), advance the start by one character to avoid unpaired surrogates.

*   Forward `AnsiOutput` (non-string PTY snapshots) to `updateOutput` immediately on every arrival, bypassing throttling.

*   Implement a trailing flush on silence:
    *   If no new text chunk arrives for longer than `OUTPUT_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` after the last flush, flush any pending buffered text automatically via `updateOutput`.

*   Schedule the trailing flush timer for the remaining time until `OUTPUT_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` has elapsed since the last flush.
    *   For example, if 750 ms have passed since the last flush, set the timer for 250 ms.

*   Cancel any pending trailing flush timer when a command exits and the exit-triggered flush fires to prevent duplicate `updateOutput` calls.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Based on my search, here's what I found regarding `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` and the shell execution buffering in gemini-cli:

## Context: The Buffer Overflow Problem

The `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` concept relates to fixing a memory/crash issue in gemini-cli's shell execution. There was a documented crash bug where the gemini instance crashes completely when running a shell command that produces a very large amount of stdout or stderr output. It appears shellExecutionService.js attempts to buffer the entire output of the executed command into a single string (stdout += decodedChunk;). If a script prints extensive logs or warnings (e.g., millions of lines in a loop), this buffer exceeds the Node.js maximum string length, causing the CLI to terminate.

The specific error was a RangeError: Invalid string length occurring in shellExecutionService.js at the line `stdout += decodedChunk;`.

## The Fix (PR #23751)

A pull request was created to address this by capping buffer sizes. It fixes a memory bloat issue where output chunks from child_process and node-pty executions were being held in memory and appended into unbounded arrays. The changes include:

- Memory Bloat Mitigation: Stops collecting chunks in the backend outputChunks array in ShellExecutionService. Instead of storing the full execution history indefinitely, it implements a constrained sniffChunks array (max 4096 bytes) used strictly for encoding detection.
- Real-time terminal progress is now tracked mathematically via a binaryBytesReceived counter instead of caching memory. Additionally, the maximum UI string concatenation lengths have been hardcapped to 1MB.

This 1MB hardcap on UI string concatenation is the concept your `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` constant refers to.

## Related Architecture Details

From the shell execution service architecture:
- Binary Detection uses isBinary() to check the first chunks of output for non-text characters, and if binary data is detected, the service stops accumulating text and reports the total bytes received.
- For PTY-based execution, it uses @xterm/headless to parse ANSI escape sequences and maintains a buffer, with a SCROLLBACK_LIMIT of 300,000 lines to ensure long-running commands do not lose output.

## Notes

The search didn't surface the exact constant name `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` verbatim in any indexed source — it appears to be an internal constant in `shellExecutionService.ts` (rather than `shell.ts`, which primarily handles command preparation, path validation, and pgrep wrapping). If you're looking at the current source, the relevant files are `packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts` (buffering/output handling) and `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts` (command wrapping/validation). For the precise current value and variable name, checking the latest source or PR #23751 directly would give you the definitive answer.

## Summary

I implemented throttled buffering for the shell tool's live output stream in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`:

**Constants & helper (module level):**
- Exported `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS = 100_000` — the max chars retained in the live buffer.
- Added `trimLiveOutputBuffer()` which keeps only the trailing `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` chars and advances the start index by one code unit when the boundary lands on a low surrogate (`0xDC00`–`0xDFFF`), avoiding unpaired surrogates.

**In `execute()`:**
- Added `trailingFlushTimer` and state (`lastUpdateTime`, `hasFlushedOutput`, `hasPendingOutput`) plus helpers:
  - `appendToLiveOutputBuffer()` — accumulates text deltas into `cumulativeOutput`, bounded via `trimLiveOutputBuffer`.
  - `flushOutput()` — cancels any pending trailing timer, then calls `updateOutput` with the buffer (guarded against no-op / background).
  - `scheduleTrailingFlush()` — schedules a flush for the *remaining* time until `OUTPUT_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` has elapsed since the last flush (e.g. 750 ms elapsed → 250 ms timer).
- Reworked the stream callback:
  - **String data chunks:** first chunk flushes immediately (`!hasFlushedOutput`); subsequent chunks within the interval accumulate and schedule a trailing flush instead of forwarding.
  - **`AnsiOutput` (non-string) chunks:** forwarded immediately every arrival, bypassing throttling.
  - **`exit`:** flushes any pending buffered text (and cancels the trailing timer) before the promise resolves.
- Added a flush after `await resultPromise` (skipped for backgrounded commands) and a `trailingFlushTimer` cleanup in the `finally` block.

The existing streaming/binary/background tests continue to pass (78 passed), and I made no changes under `tests/`.

Sources: [gemini-cli PR #23751](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/23751), [gemini-cli issue #10492](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/10492)
